steps.title: Collect soil and stone samples
steps.instruction: Collect twelve (12) soil samples and fifteen (15) stone samples, each weighing about 0.5–1.0 kg, from the land surface layer between 0 cm and 10 cm depth at the selected locations in Al Madinah, Saudi Arabia.

steps.title: Dry samples
steps.instruction: Place all collected samples in a drying oven and heat at 105 °C until completely moisture‑free.

steps.title: Quarter and homogenize
steps.instruction: Split each dried sample by the quartering method to ensure uniform elemental distribution.

steps.title: Crush and sieve
steps.instruction: Crush the quartered material and pass it through a 200‑mesh sieve to obtain a homogeneous fine powder.

steps.title: Prepare samples for gamma spectrometry
steps.instruction: For each homogenized sample, weigh an appropriate amount, transfer it into a 350 cm³ beaker, seal the beaker tightly, and store for four (4) weeks to allow secular equilibrium of radon within the sample.

steps.title: Measure gamma activity
steps.instruction: After the 4‑week sealing period, measure the activity concentrations of ²²⁶Ra, ²³²Th and ⁴⁰K in each sample using a NaI(Tl) scintillation detector (gamma spectrometry).

steps.title: Prepare XRF pellets
steps.instruction: For each powdered sample, weigh about 8 g of the powder and 1.6 g of wax, mix them, and press the mixture under suitable pressure to form solid discs suitable for X‑ray fluorescence analysis.

steps.title: Perform XRF elemental analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the pressed discs with an energy‑dispersive X‑ray fluorescence spectrometer (ARL Quant’X, Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA) to determine the oxide composition of major elements.
